acceptance_criteria: All 10 named tests pass; activation state machine correct; cargo test -p jmap-mail-server --features sieve passes
description:
Implement handle_sieve_set in src/sieve.rs (SieveScript/set handler — the complex one).

WHAT: SieveScript/set with creation, update, destruction, and the activation state machine.

ALGORITHM:
1. Parse args: extract account_id, if_in_state (Option<State>), create (Option<Map>), update (Option<Map>), destroy (Option<Vec<Id>>), on_success_activate_script (Option<String> — may be creation ref), on_success_deactivate_script (Option<bool>).
2. account_exists check.
3. ifInState check: if if_in_state is Some(s), get_state::<SieveScript>; if s != current → JmapError::state_mismatch().
4. Get old_state before mutations: backend.get_state::<SieveScript>(&account_id).await.
5. Process destroys: for each id in destroy:
   a. Fetch the script via get_objects::<SieveScript> — if isActive == true → notDestroyed with SetError::new(SetErrorType::custom("sieveIsActive"))
   b. Backend marks as VR-backed? → notDestroyed with SetError::new(SetErrorType::Forbidden)
   c. destroy_object::<SieveScript>(&account_id, &id) → Ok → add to destroyed; SetError → notDestroyed; Other → notDestroyed with serverFail
6. Process creates: for each (create_id, obj_val) in create:
   a. Deserialize to SieveScript via serde_json.
   b. blob_id must be Some and non-placeholder — else invalidProperties.
   c. get_sieve_blob(account_id, blob_id) — None → invalidProperties (blob not found); Some(bytes) → proceed.
   d. Validate script: backend.validate_sieve_script(account_id, blob_id) — Some(err) → notCreated with SetError::new(SetErrorType::custom("invalidSieve")).with_description(err).
   e. create_object::<SieveScript>(&account_id, &create_id, script) → Ok((id, obj)) → add to created; SetError (alreadyExists must include existingId) → notCreated; Other → notCreated serverFail.
7. Process updates: for each (id_str, patch) in update:
   a. If patch contains "blobId" update: get_sieve_blob + validate_sieve_script (same as create step c/d).
   b. Check if target is VR-backed AND patch touches "blobId" → notUpdated with Forbidden.
   c. update_object::<SieveScript>(&account_id, &id, patch) → Ok → updated[id] = null (or isActive value if changed); SetError → notUpdated; Other → notUpdated serverFail.
8. Activation state machine (only if ALL creates/updates/destroys have not ALL failed):
   a. If on_success_deactivate_script == Some(true): find current active script via get_objects::<SieveScript>(None) → filter isActive=true → update_object patch {"isActive": false}; if changed, add to updated map with {"isActive": false}.
   b. Resolve on_success_activate_script: if starts with '#', look up in created map; else use as-is. If id is invalid/not found → skip silently (spec §2.4). If found: update_object patch {"isActive": true}; deactivate the PREVIOUS active script first if different; add to updated map with {"isActive": true}.
9. Get new_state after all mutations.
10. Build and return response JSON (standard /set shape): oldState, newState, created, updated, destroyed, notCreated, notUpdated, notDestroyed, accountId.

DEFENSIVE RULES:
- sieveIsActive error: MUST fire when destroying active script
- alreadyExists error: MUST include existingId property
- invalidSieve error: MUST include description with line number from validator
- forbidden error: for VR-backed script destroy or blobId update
- on_success_deactivate before on_success_activate (spec §2.4)
- at-most-one-active: before activating new, deactivate old atomically
- All activation state changes MUST be reported in created/updated with new isActive value
- No .unwrap() or .expect() in production code
- Blob must be validated BEFORE creating/updating the script record

AGENT TEAM: Implementer + Tester (Tester uses spec §2.4 JSON examples 6–10 as oracles)

TESTS (oracles from spec §2.4.1 examples):
- sieve_set_create_basic: create script, verify created entry has id/name/blobId/isActive:false
- sieve_set_create_and_activate: create + onSuccessActivateScript #A → isActive:true in created
- sieve_set_at_most_one_active: two scripts exist, activate second → first deactivated (isActive:false in updated)
- sieve_set_destroy_active_rejected: sieveIsActive error
- sieve_set_destroy_inactive_ok: succeeds
- sieve_set_duplicate_name: alreadyExists with existingId
- sieve_set_deactivate_only: on_success_deactivate_script=true with no other ops → updated has isActive:false
- sieve_set_reactivate: on_success_activate_script on existing id (spec example 9)
- sieve_set_update_name: rename script, isActive unchanged
- sieve_set_unknown_account: accountNotFound
design:
Extra request args (beyond standard SetRequest):
- on_success_activate_script: Option<Id> — activate this script IFF all creates/updates/destroys succeed. Supports creation-reference (#id). Ignored if id is invalid or nonexistent.
- on_success_deactivate_script: Option<bool> — if true, deactivate the currently active script IFF all mutations succeed. Processed BEFORE on_success_activate_script (per spec §2.4).

Error types to enforce in handler (before delegating to backend):
- alreadyExists: duplicate name; response must include existingId property
- tooLarge: script size > maxSizeScript
- overQuota: would exceed maxNumberScripts
- invalidSieve: script content fails Sieve validation (backend validates on create/update since content is a blobId ref)
- sieveIsActive: attempt to destroy the active script — MUST be rejected; backend should also enforce
- forbidden: attempt to destroy or update content of the VacationResponse-backed script (§4)

Activation semantics (spec §2.4):
1. Apply all creates/updates/destroys; if any fail, stop and return errors — do NOT apply activation
2. If on_success_deactivate_script == true: deactivate current active script; add to updated with isActive: false
3. If on_success_activate_script is present and resolves to a valid id: deactivate current active (if different), activate target; add to created or updated with isActive: true
4. All activation changes reported in created/updated response args

Name uniqueness: names must be unique per account. Server-set fields: id, isActive. blobId is client-supplied (blob must already exist).

Spec ref: draft-ietf-jmap-sieve-22 §2.4, RFC 8620 §5.3.
